bugLocation: src/monitor_eval.py — evaluate(): `average = sum(values) / len(values) if values else 0`
bugSummary: an empty series is defaulted to a zero average instead of being reported as NO DATA, so a monitor whose exporter sent nothing in the window silently reads OK
minimalFix: Handle the empty case as its own status before averaging: `if not values: return "NO DATA"`, then compute `sum(values) / len(values)` only for non-empty series.
survivalStory: Guarding a division against an empty list is such a common reflex that `sum(values) / len(values) if values else 0` reads as defensive rather than buggy; it only misclassifies a series with zero in-window samples, and on the happy-path fixtures every series had data, so a zero-average-means-OK slipped through review because an empty series looks calm instead of blind.

redHerrings.looksWrongBecause: using `>=` invites the suspicion that a series whose average exactly equals its critical threshold is alerted when it should be treated as still under the limit
redHerrings.provablyInnocentBecause: the contract says a series alerts when its average is at or above its critical threshold, and db.connections averages exactly 100 against a critical threshold of 100, so `>=` correctly reports ALERT; flipping it to `>` would change that line, which is how the candidate can test it

complexityAnswer.time: O(n + m log m) for n samples and m monitored series
complexityAnswer.dominantCost: parse, dedup, group, and evaluate are each O(n); the only super-linear step is `sorted(monitors)` for output ordering at O(m log m)

debriefRubric: Reproduced with the run command and diffed against the oracle before opening the source.
Localized the wrong line to web.error_rate and named the empty series being defaulted to a zero average (and so read as OK) instead of NO DATA as the cause, in one sentence.
Shipped a minimal fix (return NO DATA for an empty series) rather than rewriting evaluate().
Complexity: identified evaluation and grouping as O(n) and the monitor sort as the only O(m log m) cost, rather than pattern-matching the division as the cost.

Phase-2: adapted by adding one WARN band after the critical check using the warning threshold already parsed onto each monitor, instead of rewriting; recognized the warning field was parsed and discarded.
Recommend exactly one drill: for a weak scoping pass, an empty/first/last boundary drill; for a weak phase-2, an adapt-vs-rewrite drill.
